key_insight: Caliper enables practical open-boundary postselection for magic state cultivation using only nondestructive mid-circuit syndrome data, narrowing the gap between idealized and implementable resource estimates.
engineering_relevance: For fault-tolerant quantum computing, this shows that realistic measurement constraints can significantly raise spacetime cost or logical error unless the escape stage and code size are redesigned.
method: Uses open-boundary postselection instead of noiseless transversal measurement
Relies on nondestructive mid-circuit syndrome information during cultivation
Targets the final escape stage to recover efficiency under practical constraints
evidence_signal: The abstract reports benchmarking across regimes where Caliper sometimes recovers prior resource efficiency, but in others prior spacetime costs correspond to logical error rates orders of magnitude worse unless larger codes and longer escape stages are used.
watch_item: Results depend on realistic mid-circuit postselection constraints, so implementations may need substantially larger codes and longer escape stages than idealized estimates suggest.
paper_title: The practical cost of magic state cultivation
